segments.source: Adriana Romero Soriano is a research scientist at Facebook AI Research and an adjunct professor at McGill University. Her research focuses on developing models and algorithms that are able to learn from multi-modal and real world data, understand and reason about conceptual relations, and recognize their uncertainties, while addressing impactful problems. She completed her postdoctoral studies at Mila, where she was advised by Prof. Yoshua Bengio. Her postdoctoral research revolved around deep learning techniques to tackle biomedical challenges, such as the ones posed by multi-modal data, high dimensional data and graph structured data. She received her Ph.D. from University of Barcelona with a thesis on assisting the training of deep neural networks with applications to computer vision, advised by Dr. Carlo Gatta. Adriana serves as program committee for conferences such as ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, and CVPR. She co-organized WiCV at CVPR 2018, RLGM at ICLR 2019, SEDL at NeurIPS 2019, the Montreal AI Symposium 2019, and SEDL at ICLR 2021.
segments.en: Biography from the original edition: Adriana Romero Soriano was a research scientist at Facebook AI Research and an adjunct professor at McGill University. Her research develops models that learn from multimodal and real-world data, reason about conceptual relationships and recognise their uncertainty while addressing meaningful problems. She completed postdoctoral research at Mila under Yoshua Bengio, applying deep learning to biomedical challenges involving multimodal, high-dimensional and graph-structured data. She received her PhD from the University of Barcelona, supervised by Carlo Gatta, with a thesis on methods to support deep neural network training for computer vision. She has served on programme committees for ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML and CVPR. She co-organised WiCV at CVPR 2018, RLGM at ICLR 2019, SEDL at NeurIPS 2019, the Montreal AI Symposium 2019 and SEDL at ICLR 2021.
segments.es: Biografía de la edición original: Adriana Romero Soriano trabajaba como investigadora en Facebook AI Research y profesora adjunta en la Universidad McGill. Su investigación busca desarrollar modelos que aprendan de datos multimodales y del mundo real, razonen sobre relaciones conceptuales y reconozcan su incertidumbre, abordando problemas relevantes. Realizó su investigación posdoctoral en Mila, bajo la supervisión de Yoshua Bengio, aplicando aprendizaje profundo a desafíos biomédicos con datos multimodales, de alta dimensión y estructurados en grafos. Obtuvo el doctorado en la Universidad de Barcelona, con una tesis sobre técnicas para facilitar el entrenamiento de redes neuronales profundas aplicadas a visión artificial, dirigida por Carlo Gatta. Ha formado parte de los comités de programa de ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML y CVPR. Coorganizó WiCV en CVPR 2018, RLGM en ICLR 2019, SEDL en NeurIPS 2019, el Montreal AI Symposium 2019 y SEDL en ICLR 2021.
